mainTopic: Does ביאה or חליצה with a pregnant יבמה count? The dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, the sources for each side, and רבא's ruling like ריש לקיש.
overview: The amud opens by finishing off a rejected answer: anyone fit for יבום is fit for חליצה, so the two cannot be split. רבא then rereads a ברייתא so that 'ביאה or חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count' applies only when the baby is viable, which fits רבי יוחנן. Another ברייתא backs רבא up, but its wording seems to refute ריש לקיש. The גמרא answers by rereading that ברייתא to fit ריש לקיש. רבי אלעזר tries to prove ריש לקיש from a משנה about a woman whose husband and צרה went overseas. That proof is rejected twice: once by giving the משנה a different reason (the worry about needing an announcement so she can marry a כהן), and once by אביי's close reading of its words. A ברייתא about a woman who miscarried after חליצה does support ריש לקיש. רבא then rules like ריש לקיש in three cases, and the amud begins the second case, about a father dividing his property as an inheritance or as a gift.

steps.title: יבום and חליצה go together
steps.stepSummary: The end of a rejection: an earlier suggestion that split ביאה and חליצה cannot stand, because whoever is fit for יבום is fit for חליצה and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because anyone who is fit for יבום is fit for חליצה, and anyone who is not fit for יבום is not fit for חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its rejection of an earlier attempt to explain the ברייתא. That attempt treated ביאה and חליצה with a pregnant woman differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule here is that יבום and חליצה always come as a pair. If a woman can do one, she can do the other. If she cannot do one, she cannot do the other. So you cannot say ביאה works but חליצה doesn't (or the reverse), and the earlier answer falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Is fit for יבום (literally, 'goes up' to יבום)
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from the brother-in-law
Levirate marriage to the dead husband's brother

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle closes off any answer that splits ביאה from חליצה. That forces רבא to find a different defense of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: that anyone who is fit for levirate marriage is fit for chalitza,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין עוֹלֶה לְיִבּוּם — אֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה לַחֲלִיצָה.
phrases.english: and anyone who is not fit for levirate marriage is not fit for chalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the rejection of a prior answer that came before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier suggestion that ביאה and חליצה of a pregnant woman are treated differently.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It breaks the rule that fitness for יבום and fitness for חליצה always go together.

steps.title: רבא rereads the ברייתא as talking about a viable baby
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא's rule that ביאה and חליצה of a pregnant woman don't count applies only when the baby is viable. The baby frees the family only once it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what the ברייתא means. Someone marries his יבמה through יבום, and then it turns out she was pregnant. Her צרה may not remarry, in case the baby is viable. ביאה with a pregnant woman is not considered ביאה, and חליצה with a pregnant woman is not considered חליצה. And the baby does not free them until it comes out into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to defend רבי יוחנן. He explains the ברייתא so it no longer clashes with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says ביאה and חליצה with a pregnant woman don't count. רבא says this only applies when the baby is viable. In that case the dead brother had a child, so there was never any יבום at all. If the baby is not viable, the ביאה or חליצה does count, exactly as רבי יוחנן holds. Even a viable baby only frees the women once it is actually born.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries his יבמה through יבום
Her co-wife (צרה), the dead brother's other wife
A viable baby, one who will live
Frees someone from the bond of יבום

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'ביאת מעוברת לא שמה ביאה' sound like a blanket rule. In רבא's reading they only apply when the baby turns out to be viable.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said, this is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the ברייתא discussed before this section.

phrases.english: One who marries his yevama, and she is found to be pregnant —
her rival wife may not marry,
lest the baby be viable.
And intercourse with a pregnant woman is not called intercourse,
phrases.notes: In רבא's reading, he means a woman carrying a viable baby.

phrases.english: and chalitza of a pregnant woman is not called chalitza.
And the baby does not release
until it comes out into the air of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was just rejected with a new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the ברייתא is limited to a case where the baby is viable.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that ביאה or חליצה with any pregnant woman never counts, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only fails to count when the baby is viable. When the baby is not viable it counts, which fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא that matches רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that matches רבא's reading. When the baby is viable, the baby is what frees the women, not the ביאה or חליצה, and only once it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches רבא. Someone marries his יבמה through יבום, and then it turns out she was pregnant. Her צרה may not remarry, in case the baby is viable. Neither ביאה nor חליצה frees her; only the baby frees her. And the baby does not free her until it comes out into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says outright what רבא said. The only worry is that the baby might be viable, and in that case the baby frees the women, not the ביאה or חליצה. This backs up the idea that the 'doesn't count' rule is tied to a viable baby.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
Into the air of the world, meaning actually born

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא and this ברייתא, a viable baby frees the women, but only once it is born. ביאה or חליצה only fails to count when the baby is viable.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rava:
One who marries his yevama, and she is found to be pregnant —
her rival wife may not marry,
lest the baby be viable,
and intercourse or chalitza does not release,
rather, the baby releases.
And the baby does not release her
until it comes out into the air of the world.

steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that the ruling depends on whether the baby is viable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the only worry is a viable baby, and that the baby is what frees the women.

steps.title: Does this ברייתא refute ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's reason, the גמרא infers that if the baby is not viable, the צרה is freed. That suggests the ביאה counted, and it looks like a refutation of ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is only that the baby might be viable. That means that if the baby is not viable, her צרה is freed. Should we then say this is a refutation of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא's reason and points out that it seems to go against ריש לקיש. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only worries about a viable baby. So if the baby is not viable, the ביאה did free the צרה. ריש לקיש holds that ביאה with a pregnant woman never counts, even when the baby is not viable. So the ברייתא seems to disprove him.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies that (it opens an inference from the opposite case)
Shall we say this is a refutation?

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' means 'shall we say.' It raises the challenge as a possibility, and the גמרא may still go on to answer it.

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּשֶׁמָּא יְהֵא וָלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא הוּא,
phrases.english: The reason is that the baby might be viable;

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא הָוֵי וָלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא
phrases.english: this implies that if the baby is not viable,
her rival wife is released.
Shall we say this is a refutation of Reish Lakish!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּשֶׁמָּא יְהֵא וָלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 3 to challenge the other side of the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that ביאה or חליצה with a pregnant woman is never valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives only one reason, that the baby might be viable. So if the baby is not viable, the צרה is freed, which means the ביאה counted.

steps.title: ריש לקיש rereads the ברייתא: the צרה may not marry
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the ברייתא actually says the צרה may NOT marry, because the baby might not be viable, and ביאה or חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש could answer you: this is what the ברייתא means. If a man marries his יבמה and she turns out to be pregnant, her צרה may not marry. Maybe the baby will not be viable. And חליצה with a pregnant woman is not real חליצה, and ביאה with a pregnant woman is not real ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by reading the ברייתא in a new way that fits his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 read the ברייתא as saying the צרה goes free if the baby is not viable. ריש לקיש reads it the other way: the צרה is stuck, because if the baby is not viable, the ביאה done during the pregnancy never counted. So the last line of the ברייתא now supports ריש לקיש instead of challenging him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching (introduces a new reading of a source)
One who marries his brother's widow through יבום
A co-wife (another wife of the same dead husband)
A viable baby, one that will live

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. In step 4 the ברייתא seemed to free the צרה. In ריש לקיש's reading the צרה is NOT free; she must wait.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish could say to you:
This is what the baraita is teaching:
One who marries his yevama and she turns out to be pregnant —
her rival wife may not marry,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא יְהֵא הַוָּלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא,
phrases.english: since perhaps the baby will not be viable,
and chalitza with a pregnant woman is not called chalitza,
and intercourse with a pregnant woman is not called intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies that if the baby is not viable, the צרה is free, so the ביאה counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really says the צרה may not marry, because if the baby is not viable, the ביאה or חליצה during the pregnancy did not count.

steps.title: Even though most babies are viable, a baby frees only once born
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the last line of the ברייתא: you might want to rely on the majority of viable babies, but a baby only frees the family once it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: go after the majority of women, and most women give birth to a healthy, viable baby, so let her marry. The answer is that a baby does not free anyone until it comes out into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains why the ברייתא needs its final line about the baby being born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue the צרה should be allowed to marry now, since most babies are viable and a viable baby frees everyone. The ברייתא blocks this: the baby frees no one until birth. So until then, she needs a ביאה or חליצה that counts, and during the pregnancy there is no such thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Majority; we usually follow what is most common
The air of the world, meaning after birth

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, during the pregnancy nothing frees the צרה. The ביאה or חליצה doesn't count, and the baby doesn't help until it is born.

phrases.english: And if you say:
Follow the majority of women,
and most women give birth to a healthy, viable baby,
a baby does not free the women
until it comes out into the air of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes ריש לקיש's rereading by explaining the ברייתא's final clause
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why a clause is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since most babies are viable, the צרה could marry right away.
steps.terutzMaskana: A baby frees no one until birth, so the majority does not help now.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר finds a משנה hinting at ריש לקיש's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר feels that ריש לקיש's rule must be hinted at in a משנה. He searches and finds the משנה of a woman whose husband and צרה went overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Could ריש לקיש's teaching be true and we never learned it in a משנה? He went out, searched carefully, and found it. We learned: A woman's husband and her צרה went overseas. People came and told her, 'Your husband died.' She may not marry, and she may not do יבום, until she finds out whether her צרה is pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a משנה that he will use to support ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the woman wait until she knows whether her צרה is pregnant, and it does not even let her do יבום. רבי אלעזר will now show that this waiting only makes full sense if ריש לקיש is right.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Is it possible that this teaching of Reish Lakish is true
and we did not learn it in a mishna?
He went out, looked carefully, and found it,
as we learned:

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ וְצָרָתָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.english: A woman whose husband and rival wife went overseas,
and people came and told her, "Your husband died" —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זוֹ לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא וְלֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם
phrases.english: she may not marry and may not do yibum

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתֵּדַע שֶׁמָּא מְעוּבֶּרֶת הִיא צָרָתָהּ.
phrases.english: until she knows whether perhaps her rival wife is pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֶפְשָׁר אִיתָא לְהָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ וְלָא תְּנַן לָהּ בְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending ריש לקיש, the גמרא now looks for positive support for him in a משנה
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that ביאה and חליצה with a pregnant woman do not count
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of a woman whose husband and צרה went overseas

steps.title: Why may she not do חליצה? Starting to analyze the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר starts working through the משנה. Forbidding יבום is understandable, but why forbid חליצה? Within the nine months it is clear, because the situation is still in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that she may not do יבום: maybe the baby will be viable, and then the brother would break the Torah ban on a brother's wife. But why may she not do חליצה? It makes sense that she can't do חליצה within nine months and marry within nine months, because that is still a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר starts to show how the משנה supports ריש לקיש. This step sets up the next move, which will ask about after the nine months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום is clearly forbidden: if the baby is viable, the brother never had a מצוה and he would be with his brother's wife. חליצה seems harmless, so רבי אלעזר asks why the משנה forbids it. He grants that within nine months the outcome is still unknown. That leaves the real question for after nine months, which is where ריש לקיש's rule will come in.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (granted), usually followed by 'but' (אֶלָּא)
A brother's wife, forbidden unless there is a מצוה of יבום

phrases.english: It makes sense that she may not do yibum —
perhaps the baby will be viable,
and he will run into the Torah prohibition of a brother's wife,
But why may she not do chalitza?
It makes sense that she may not do chalitza within nine months
and marry within nine months —
no, because that is a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא יַבּוֹמֵי לָא, שֶׁמָּא יְהֵא וָלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins drawing the proof for ריש לקיש out of the משנה quoted in step 7
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that חליצה of a pregnant woman does not count
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ban on חליצה, explained step by step: the ban on יבום is clear, and the ban within nine months is due to doubt

steps.title: רבי אלעזר finishes his proof: why not do חליצה during the nine months?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks why the משנה does not let her do חליצה within the nine months and then marry after them. The only answer he sees is that חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count, which supports ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her do חליצה within the nine months, and marry after the nine months!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר finishes the argument he started in step 8. He shows there was an easy option the משנה ignored, and that this points to ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she did חליצה during the nine months and married after them, every outcome would be safe. A viable baby means there was never a יבום bond. A non-viable baby means the חליצה freed her. The משנה does not allow this, so רבי אלעזר concludes the חליצה must not count while the צרה might be pregnant.

phrases.english: But let her perform חליצה within the nine months,
and marry after the nine months.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the conclusion unsaid: since the משנה doesn't allow this, חליצה with a pregnant woman must not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אלעזר's reading of the משנה begun in step 8
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that ביאה or חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה forbids חליצה even though doing it within the nine months and marrying afterward would seem to solve everything

steps.title: Even on that view, she could do both after nine months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even if חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count, the משנה should still allow her to do חליצה and marry after nine months. So the משנה's strictness is not explained by ריש לקיש's rule either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning: let her do חליצה and marry after nine months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבי אלעזר's question back on him. His own explanation leaves the same kind of problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After nine months the pregnancy question is over, so even ריש לקיש would agree that חליצה works then. The משנה does not offer that option either. This means the משנה's ruling comes from some other concern, and it proves nothing about ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: your own view has the same problem

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning:
let her perform חליצה and marry after nine months!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה for ריש לקיש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ריש לקיש's rule does not explain why the משנה forbids חליצה even after nine months, so the משנה must have a different reason

steps.title: The real reason for the משנה: she might end up needing an announcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the משנה aside as a proof. It explains, in the name of אביי בר אבא and רב חיננא בר אביי, that the worry is a viable baby. Then the חליצה would have been meaningless, and an announcement would be needed so she could still marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, leave that משנה aside. Its reason is as אביי בר אבא and רב חיננא בר אביי both say: perhaps the baby will be viable, and you will end up needing an announcement that she may marry into כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the משנה is not evidence for either side. It gives the true reason the משנה forbids חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the צרה's baby is viable, there was never a יבום bond. Then the חליצה meant nothing, and she may still marry a כהן. But people saw a חליצה and will think of her as a חלוצה, who is forbidden to a כהן. To fix this, a public announcement would be needed. The משנה avoids the whole problem by not allowing the חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave that one aside: that source proves nothing here
A viable baby, one who will live

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the משנה as a source for ריש לקיש. A ברייתא that does support him comes in step 15, and רבא rules like him in step 16.

phrases.english: Rather, leave that one aside.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַבָּיֵי בַּר אַבָּא וְרַב חִינָּנָא בַּר אַבָּיֵי
phrases.english: For Abaye bar Abba and Rav Ḥinnana bar Abaye
both say:
perhaps the baby will be viable,
and it will turn out that you require for her
an announcement for the priesthood.
phrases.notes: The announcement would tell everyone that the חליצה was meaningless, so she may still marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the proof, gives the real reason for the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה with a different concern that has nothing to do with whether the חליצה counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids חליצה because חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids חליצה because a viable baby would make it meaningless, and an announcement would then be needed to allow her to marry a כהן

steps.title: So what? Just make the announcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why needing an announcement is a problem. Let her do חליצה, and if the baby is viable, simply announce that she may marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let us require an announcement for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave. An announcement seems like an easy fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that a viable baby would leave a mistaken image of her as a חלוצה. A public announcement would clear that up, so why should this stop the חליצה?

keyTerms.meaning: So let us require it for her

phrases.english: So let us require it for her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that needing an announcement is a reason to forbid the חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An announcement solves the problem, so there is no need to forbid the חליצה

steps.title: Not everyone hears the announcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that some people may have seen the חליצה but missed the announcement. Those people would think the court is letting a חלוצה marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps there is someone who was at the חליצה but not at the announcement, and he will come to say: they permit a חלוצה to a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why an announcement is not good enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An announcement only reaches the people who hear it. Anyone who saw the חליצה but missed the announcement would think the rabbis allow a חלוצה to marry a כהן. That is why the משנה forbids the חליצה from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: The act of making a public announcement
A woman who has done חליצה, forbidden to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove ריש לקיש's rule. It forbids חליצה during a possible pregnancy for a different reason. A viable baby would make the חליצה meaningless, and fixing her status with an announcement is unreliable, because some witnesses of the חליצה would never hear it.

phrases.english: Perhaps there is a person
who was at the חליצה
and was not at the announcement,
and he will come to say:
they are permitting a חלוצה to a כהן.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the suggested fix does not work in practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A public announcement would solve the problem of her looking like a חלוצה
steps.terutzMaskana: Some people who saw the חליצה will miss the announcement and think a חלוצה was allowed to marry a כהן

steps.title: אביי rereads the משנה so it proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה never forbade חליצה. It only forbade marrying someone else without חליצה, so it gives no support to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Does the משנה say 'she may not do חליצה and may not do יבום'? It says 'she may not marry and may not do יבום.' That means she may not marry without חליצה. But if he does חליצה with her, she really is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another way to push away רבי אלעזר's proof. He looks closely at the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר assumed the משנה forbids חליצה during pregnancy and asked why. אביי says the משנה never said that. Its words 'לא תנשא' only forbid marrying without a חליצה. So if the יבם did do חליצה, she may marry after the nine months, and the question that led to the proof is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach...? A way of saying the text does not actually say this

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying חליצה during pregnancy works. He is only saying the משנה does not prove that it fails. The support for ריש לקיש comes instead from the ברייתא in the next step.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: 'To him' means to רבי אלעזר, who brought the proof from the משנה.

phrases.english: Does it teach 'she may not do חליצה and may not do יבום'?
It teaches 'she may not marry and may not do יבום,'
meaning without חליצה,
but if he does חליצה with her,
she really is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִידֵּי ״לֹא תַּחְלוֹץ וְלֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second, separate rejection of רבי אלעזר's proof from step 9. It works through the wording of the משנה instead of the reasoning in steps 11 to 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the use of the משנה as proof for ריש לקיש. It does not reject ריש לקיש's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה forbids חליצה during pregnancy. In fact it only forbids marrying without חליצה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a pregnant woman had חליצה and then miscarried, she needs a new חליצה. So the first חליצה did not count, just as ריש לקיש says.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with ריש לקיש: One who does חליצה with a pregnant woman, and she then miscarries, she needs חליצה from the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: After the משנה failed as a proof, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that clearly supports ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby is not born alive, she was a יבמה all along and needs a valid חליצה. The ברייתא requires a new one, so the חליצה done while she was pregnant did not count. That is exactly ריש לקיש's position.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real source support for ריש לקיש, and it prepares the way for רבא's ruling in the next step.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with ריש לקיש:
One who does חליצה with a pregnant woman, and she miscarried,
she needs חליצה from the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה was rejected as a proof in step 14. Now a ברייתא gives the support that the משנה could not.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: after a miscarriage she needs a new חליצה from the brothers.

steps.title: רבא rules like ריש לקיש in three cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows ריש לקיש in three disputes. The first is the one just discussed, חליצה with a pregnant woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows ריש לקיש in these three. One is the one we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the practical ruling for our סוגיא. He also begins a list of other places where the הלכה follows ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this, the חליצה dispute is settled: חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count. רבא then starts to list his other cases, so the גמרא is about to bring a new source.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows ריש לקיש: חליצה done with a pregnant woman does not count. If she miscarries, she needs a new חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole discussion about the pregnant יבמה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The הלכה follows ריש לקיש
in these three:
One is the one we just said.
phrases.notes: He means the dispute about חליצה with a pregnant woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּהָנֵי תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא supports ריש לקיש, רבא rules in his favor.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows ריש לקיש: חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count.

steps.title: The second case: dividing property by word of mouth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. A father divides his property among his sons out loud, giving some more and some less, or giving the firstborn the same share as the others. His words stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one is from what we learned in a משנה: One who divides his property by word of mouth, giving more to one and less to another, or making the firstborn equal to them, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on רבא's second case by quoting the משנה that it is based on. This sets up a later discussion of what ריש לקיש says about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a completely new topic, the laws of inheritance and gifts. The משנה says a man can divide his property unequally, and can even take away the firstborn's extra share, and it works. The גמרא has not yet said what the dispute is.

phrases.english: The other one is what we learned in a משנה:
One who divides his property by word of mouth,
giving more to one and less to another,
or making the firstborn equal to them,
phrases.notes: The firstborn normally gets a double share. Here the father gives him the same share as his brothers.

phrases.english: his words stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִידַּךְ, דִּתְנַן: הַמְחַלֵּק נְכָסָיו עַל פִּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This fills in the second item on רבא's list of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father who divides his property unequally by word of mouth, even taking away the firstborn's extra share, is bound by his words.

steps.title: Calling it inheritance versus calling it a gift
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If he says the unequal shares are an inheritance, his words mean nothing. If he writes anywhere in the document that they are a gift, his words stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said it was as an inheritance, he has said nothing. If he wrote, whether at the beginning, the end, or the middle, that it was as a gift, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. It shows that the label he uses, inheritance or gift, makes all the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance shares are set by the Torah, so a man cannot change them by calling his own division 'inheritance.' A gift is his own choice to make. So if the word 'gift' appears anywhere in what he wrote, the division works.

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing (his words have no effect)
Whether at the beginning or at the end

steps.confusionAlert: The same unequal division can fail or work depending only on whether he calls it 'inheritance' or 'gift.'

phrases.english: But if he said it was as an inheritance,
he has said nothing.
phrases.notes: His words have no effect, because he cannot change the Torah's inheritance shares.

phrases.english: If he wrote, whether at the beginning,
or at the end, or in the middle,
that it was as a gift,
his words stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר מִשּׁוּם יְרוּשָּׁה — לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unequal division called 'inheritance' has no effect. One called a 'gift' anywhere in the document is binding.
